parameters.jsCode: const body=$input.first().json.body;const required=['source_document','document_type'];const missing=required.filter(f=>!body[f]);if(missing.length)return[{json:{valid:false,error:'Missing: '+missing.join(', ')}}];if(body.source_document.trim().length<200)return[{json:{valid:false,error:'source_document too short — this tool is for condensing substantial documents'}}];const docTypes=['research_report','technical_spec','financial_analysis','market_research','project_status','strategy_doc','legal_document','meeting_notes','other'];const docType=docTypes.includes(body.document_type)?body.document_type:'other';const lengths=['one_paragraph','half_page','one_page'];const targetLength=lengths.includes(body.target_length)?body.target_length:'half_page';return[{json:{valid:true,sourceDocument:body.source_document.trim().slice(0,15000),documentType:docType,targetLength,audience:(body.audience||'').slice(0,200),focusAreas:Array.isArray(body.focus_areas)?body.focus_areas:(body.focus_areas||'').split(',').map(f=>f.trim()).filter(Boolean),decisionNeeded:(body.decision_needed||'').slice(0,300),replyEmail:body.reply_email||null}}];

values.content: You condense long documents into executive summaries for busy readers. Good executive summaries lead with the bottom line, include only what a decision-maker needs to know, quantify where the source does, flag what's uncertain or contested in the source, and are honest about what got cut. You never fabricate content not present in the source. You paraphrase in your own words rather than lifting sentences verbatim. Always respond in valid JSON only.
